notes: v1.14.554 — LEGACY-RETIRE STAGE 7b: THE LEGACY CHROME IS GONE, AND WITH IT STAGE 7. The 5-tab nav (markup, CSS, and the tn_setupSpineObserver IIFE that existed only to sync its capsule and ribbon), the legacy header chevron #nav-back-btn (markup, CSS, nav_updateBackButton and both call sites), and the --tabnav-h token are all deleted. ⛔ THE TOKEN COULD NOT SIMPLY BE DELETED: seven live declarations read it, and Contract 15 is explicit that an undefined var() silently invalidates the WHOLE declaration. All seven are repointed to --rd-navclear first. ⭐ That is not a rename, it is a FIX: --tabnav-h was 72px while the real nav measures ~122px, so those seven paddings had been under-paying their clearance — the same stale-constant defect .341 and .532 record, still live on .page, #page-search, .sop-detail and the two master surfaces. --rd-navclear is measured at runtime by rd_syncNavClear, and it inherits from body.rd, which is now always applied. One occurrence is deliberately LEFT: a v1.14.282 historical note that describes what the dock USED to read. Rewriting it would have made the note false. VISIBLE: those five surfaces gain roughly 50px of bottom clearance, which is the correction, not a regression.
